case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread discusses updating Bluetooth SIG qualification registrations for an existing product after Host Subsystem and Profile Subsystem changes caused by an Android OS update. The company wants to reuse historical test evidence generated by another test facility and determine whether it remains valid under upcoming qualification requirements. A review of the legacy RF and RF PHY reports identified a missing RF PHY test case that should have been present at the time of the original qualification. The discussion focuses on whether additional testing is necessary, how qualification updates can be performed with minimal risk, and how supplier-provided design updates can resolve qualification concerns.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The main technical issue is whether existing RF and RF PHY test reports can be reused when updating Host and Profile layers in a new qualification submission. Review of the legacy evidence found one required RF PHY test case missing from the original report, likely due to a test facility oversight. Because the original Controller qualification had already been approved, the consultant explained that including the existing qualified Controller design without modifying its ICS would not trigger new RF PHY testing requirements. The thread also analyzes how modifying RF PHY ICS data to incorporate additional test evidence could trigger inter-layer consistency checks and create new qualification risks. Later discussion confirms that supplier-created subset designs removing unsupported power-class functionality resolve previously identified inter-layer concerns.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant's reasoning is based on preserving the already approved qualified design and avoiding unnecessary modifications that would trigger new qualification obligations. Since the existing Controller design was formally accepted by the Bluetooth SIG, the missing RF PHY test item is treated as effectively covered for the purpose of the update path. Reusing the approved design unchanged while updating only the intended Host and Profile references minimizes testing exposure and avoids additional consistency-check failures. Supplier-provided subset designs are preferred because they remove problematic capabilities without forcing broader reassessment of the qualification hierarchy.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: If the qualification update is handled incorrectly, unnecessary RF PHY testing and additional qualification activities may be triggered. Modifying ICS content solely to inject missing test evidence can cause inter-layer dependency checks to run and may expose new inconsistencies between Controller, Host, and Profile layers. This can create avoidable qualification risk, additional engineering effort, and schedule impact. The thread also notes that a paid supplemental test effort could be incurred even though the underlying issue appears to stem from an earlier test facility oversight.
case_analysis.consulting_mistake: A legacy qualification report was found to be missing a required RF PHY test case that should already have been been included when the original design was qualified. The consultant attributes this to a test facility verification error and recommends pursuing corrective action with the original test provider rather than unnecessarily requalifying the design.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When updating Bluetooth qualifications that rely on previously approved designs, first determine whether the desired registration path can reuse existing qualified layers unchanged. Avoid making unnecessary ICS modifications solely to correct historical evidence gaps, because doing so may trigger new testing and inter-layer validation requirements. Always evaluate whether supplier subset designs or existing approved qualifications can resolve the issue with lower qualification risk.
